name: Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park
blurb: Remote Sulu Sea atolls where sharks, turtles and manta rays patrol pristine coral.

tip.title: Remove the Napoleon wrasse
tip.text: Napoleon wrasse eat crown-of-thorns starfish, among other prey. Set Napoleon wrasse to -100% and watch the starfish rise, then the corals and everything that lives on them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Shallow, clear water lets light reach the corals and algae on the atolls, driving photosynthesis on the reef.
Dissolved nutrients from mixing water and recycled waste are scarce in tropical seas and limit algae and plankton.

nodes.name: Bacteria & microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead coral tissue, algae, plankton and animal remains, returning nutrients to the water.
Drifting microscopic algae at the base of the open-water food chain, eaten by zooplankton.
Hard corals that build the reef and host symbiotic algae; they feed partly on sunlight and partly on plankton. Habitat for most reef species.

nodes.name: Halimeda and reef algae
nodes.desc: Calcified green algae that grow on reef rock and sand, grazed by reef fish and turtles.
Tiny drifting animals that graze phytoplankton and feed fusiliers and manta rays.
Algae-grazing reef fish that keep algae from overgrowing coral.
A grazing turtle that eats algae and seagrass and nests on the sandy islets of the atolls.

nodes.name: Hawksbill turtle
nodes.desc: A reef turtle that eats mainly sponges plus algae and other reef animals; it also nests on the atoll islets.
A starfish that feeds on live coral; outbreaks can strip large areas of reef, and one was reported at Tubbataha in 2009.
A filter-feeding ray that strains zooplankton from the water and visits reef cleaning stations.
A powerful reef predator that hunts fish in the reef and lagoon.
A plunge-diving seabird that nests on the islets and feeds on fish and squid.
A large shark reported at Tubbataha and named among its top predators; it eats fish, turtles and many other prey.
